chapter: Royal Roost, Birdland and Three O'Clock High
title: Three O'Clock High: booking Sunday concerts without agents
summary: With Art Blakey he formed a company that booked stars directly for Sunday concerts, mostly losing money.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Birdland with Art Tatum, and also played on the same bill as Ella Fitzgerald. I worked with her there. But Art Blackey at this time, one night, came up to me with an idea of doing some booking of -- we were going to -- we got a little corporation called Three O'clock High. Now, this --
What was the significance of the name?

I don't know, I really don't know because we were all the time high. You know. But any way we would -- actually what we did was create jobs for musicians. Now, the premise behind the whole thing was for us to get to the star rather than to the agent, so I knew everybody in show business. Okay. So we would book this thing on Sundays, you know, like a little concert on Sundays, and on any Sunday I might have Art Tatum, Errol with his group, Bird with his group. Because they wouldn't charge me -- I'm not going through the office to get these people, see. So I would just tell them, look, this is what we're trying to do, just really trying to create some work for some of the guys, would you come. And so they'd say, yeah, John, give me -- Errol would say, look, just pay Shadow and John Simmons. He wouldn't even take any money. You know.
